questions.stem: I ______ the film yesterday. But I ______ it before yesterday.
questions.explanation: 第一空有明确过去时间状语yesterday，必须用一般过去时saw；第二空before yesterday表示"昨天之前"，是从过去持续到现在的时间段，且与现在有关（昨天看了，昨天之前没看过），用现在完成时haven't seen。B选项时态颠倒，C选项第二空时态错误，D选项第一空时态错误。
questions.label: 语法题

questions.stem: The girl ______ is standing under the tree is my sister.
questions.explanation: 先行词the girl指人，且在定语从句中作主语（is standing），所以用who。which用于指物；whom用于指人但作宾语；whose表示"谁的"，在从句中作定语。句意：站在树下的那个女孩是我妹妹。
questions.label: 语法题

questions.stem: The bridge ______ by the workers last year.
questions.explanation: 主语the bridge与build是被动关系（桥被建），且时间状语last year表示过去，所以用一般过去时的被动语态was built。A是主动语态现在时；B是主动语态过去时；D是被动语态现在时，时态不符。
questions.label: 语法题

questions.stem: —______ you ever ______ to the Great Wall? —Yes, I ______ there with my parents last summer.
questions.explanation: 第一空ever是现在完成时标志词，问"曾经去过吗"用have been to；第二空last summer是过去时间，用一般过去时went。have gone to表示"去了某地（未回）"，不符合语境；A选项第一空助动词错误；C、D选项第二空时态错误。
questions.label: 语法题

questions.stem: Please ______ the lights when you leave the classroom.
questions.explanation: turn off表示"关闭（电器等）"，符合句意"离开教室时请关灯"。turn on打开；turn up调高（音量等）；turn down调低或拒绝。根据leave the classroom的语境，应该是关灯。
questions.label: 词汇题

questions.stem: The news is ______. I feel very ______ about it.
questions.explanation: surprising表示"令人惊讶的"，修饰物（the news）；surprised表示"感到惊讶的"，修饰人（I）。句意：这个消息令人惊讶。我对它感到很惊讶。ing形容词描述事物特性，ed形容词描述人的感受。
questions.label: 词汇题

questions.stem: We should ______ our best to protect the environment.
questions.explanation: try one's best是固定搭配，表示"尽某人最大努力"。do one's best也是正确搭配，但选项B是do，没有所有格our；make和give不与best构成此含义的固定搭配。
questions.label: 词汇题

questions.explanation: 根据下文"didn't want to take part in it"（不想参加）可知，起初学生认为这个活动很"无聊"。boring令人无聊的；interesting有趣的（与下文态度矛盾）；necessary必要的（不能解释不想参加）；possible可能的（不符合语境）。
questions.label: 完形填空
questions.group_passage:
Last month, our school started a green project called "Zero Waste Campus". The goal was to help students understand the importance of environmental protection and develop good habits.

Every class was asked to collect plastic bottles and waste paper. At first, many students thought it was (8)______ and didn't want to take part in it. However, after the teacher explained how much waste we produced every day, we realized that our small actions could make a big (9)______.

My class decided to do something different. We set up a recycling corner in our classroom. Students brought used books and stationery from home. These items were then (10)______ to other students who needed them. This not only reduced waste but also helped those who couldn't afford new school things.

After two months, the results were amazing. The amount of waste in our school dropped by 30%. The headmaster was (11)______ with our efforts and praised us in the school meeting. He said this project had changed the way we think about waste.

Now, recycling has become a part of our daily life. I believe if everyone takes action, we can create a (12)______ world for future generations. This experience has taught me that environmental protection starts with small steps.

questions.explanation: make a difference是固定短语，表示"产生影响、起作用"。句意：我们意识到我们的小行动可以产生重大影响。make a mistake犯错误；make a decision做决定；make a change做出改变（通常说make changes或make a big change）。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what should you do first when using the memory palace technique?
options: A. Walk through your house physically
questions.explanation: 细节理解题。根据第二段"First, choose a place you know very well, such as your home"可知，第一步是选择一个你非常熟悉的地方。A选项是物理上走过房子，而文中说的是imagine（想象）；C是举例中的细节；D是另一个方法的内容。
questions.label: 阅读-细节理解
questions.group_passage:
Do you often forget things? Many students complain that they can't remember new English words or historical dates. In fact, memory is like a muscle - the more you use it, the stronger it becomes. Scientists have found some effective ways to improve memory.

One popular method is called the "memory palace" technique. This method has been used for thousands of years. Here's how it works: First, choose a place you know very well, such as your home. Then, imagine you are walking through it. Place the things you want to remember at different spots (locations) in your mind. For example, if you need to remember a shopping list, you might put apples on your bed and milk on your desk. When you need to recall the list, just take a mental walk through your house.

Another useful tip is to review information at regular intervals (间隔). Instead of studying for five hours straight, it's better to study for one hour a day over five days. This gives your brain time to process and store the information properly.

Sleep also plays an important role in memory. During sleep, your brain organizes the information you learned during the day. That's why pulling an all-nighter (熬夜) before an exam is usually not effective.

So next time you struggle to remember something, try these methods. With practice, you'll find that remembering things becomes much easier.

questions.stem: What can we infer from the passage about studying?
options: A. Studying for long hours without breaks is the best way
B. Sleeping less helps improve memory
C. Short regular study sessions are more effective than cramming
D. The memory palace only works for shopping lists
questions.explanation: 推理判断题。根据第三段"Instead of studying for five hours straight, it's better to study for one hour a day over five days"可知，分散的短时学习比长时间连续学习（填鸭式学习）更有效。A与文意相反；B与第四段强调睡眠重要性相悖；D过于绝对，文中只是用购物清单举例。

Many students have trouble balancing their schoolwork and hobbies. They often feel stressed because they don't have enough time for both. However, with proper planning, you can enjoy both without sacrificing your grades. (17)______
